seo.title: U.S. Furniture Export FAQ: Canada & Mexico Tariffs, HS Codes

intro: Short answers to what people search about exporting U.S. furniture, seats, mattresses and lighting, each drawn from the other export pages of this report.
keyTakeaways: Canada charges U.S. household seats, kitchen cabinets, bedroom, metal and plastic furniture and LED fixtures 25% or 50% since September 8, 2026; seat parts, mattresses and medical furniture still enter free under CUSMA.
Mexico (USMCA), the EU (since July 1, 2026) and Australia (AUSFTA) let U.S. furniture in free; China adds 10% to its normal rate.
Most Chapter 94 goods are EAR99; the HS code, the first six digits of the Schedule B number, is 9401 for seats, 9403 for furniture, 9404 for mattresses and 9405 for lighting.

faqs.question: Does Canada have tariffs on U.S. furniture?
faqs.answer: Yes, on much of it. Since September 8, 2026 Canada's United States Surtax Order (2026) charges 50% on U.S. office swivel chairs, metal-frame seats, other metal furniture, wooden bedroom and other wooden furniture, plastic furniture and LED light fixtures, and 25% on upholstered wooden-frame sofas and chairs, wooden kitchen cabinets and wooden furniture parts, with no CUSMA exemption. Since December 26, 2025 a separate 25% global surtax also covers U.S. steel office furniture, other furniture parts and prefabricated buildings.
searchedAs: does canada have tariffs on us furniture

faqs.question: Is there duty on furniture shipped from the USA to Canada?
faqs.answer: U.S.-made furniture that qualifies under CUSMA pays no Canadian customs duty (the normal rate is 8–9.5% on household furniture). The cost comes from Canada's surtaxes, charged on goods of U.S. origin whether or not they qualify for CUSMA: 25% or 50% on most household seats, cabinets, bedroom, metal and plastic furniture and LED fixtures, and 25% on steel office furniture and prefabricated buildings. Seat parts, motor-vehicle seats, medical furniture, mattresses and bedding pay neither.

faqs.question: What did Canada's September 8, 2026 tariffs do to U.S. kitchen cabinets and lighting?
faqs.answer: Canada answered the U.S. Section 338 tariffs with counter-tariffs of 15%, 25% and 50% on listed U.S. goods from September 8, 2026. Wooden kitchen furniture such as cabinets (9403.40) pays 25%, and LED ceiling and wall fittings and other LED luminaires (9405.11, 9405.42) and lamp parts pay 50%. A $1 million shipment of U.S. kitchen cabinets now pays $250,000, against nothing in January 2025.
searchedAs: did canada put tariffs on us goods

faqs.question: Does Mexico charge tariffs on U.S. furniture?
faqs.answer: Not on U.S. furniture that qualifies under USMCA: it enters Mexico free, and Mexico has published no counter-tariff on U.S. goods. From January 1, 2026 Mexico raised its general rates on most seats, furniture and mattress supports to 25% or 35% (other metal furniture went from 7% to 35%), so goods that fail the USMCA origin rules now pay much more.

current mexico tariffs on us goods

faqs.question: Does China have tariffs on U.S. furniture?
faqs.answer: Yes. China's normal rate on furniture is 0%, but it adds a 10% extra tariff to every U.S. good, so a $1 million shipment of U.S. office or bedroom furniture pays $100,000. Mattresses and bedding pay 10% plus 10%, LED fixtures 6–10% plus 10%. The extra tariff would rise to 34% if China's suspension ends on January 10, 2027.

does china have tariffs on us products
does china have tariffs on us

faqs.question: What do the EU and the UK charge on U.S. furniture?
faqs.answer: Since July 1, 2026 the EU charges 0% on every U.S. Chapter 94 good under Regulation (EU) 2026/1455, until December 31, 2029; before, seat parts paid up to 2.7%, bedding 3.7% and lamps up to 4.7%. The UK charges its normal UK Global Tariff: most finished furniture is free and seats, bedding and lamps pay 0–4%.
searchedAs: eu tariffs on us goods list

faqs.question: What is the HS code for furniture parts?
faqs.answer: Parts of seats are 9401.91 if of wood and 9401.99 otherwise; parts of other furniture are 9403.91 if of wood and 9403.99 otherwise. Parts of medical furniture stay in 9402 and lamp parts are 9405.91 to 9405.99. These six digits are also the start of the 10-digit Schedule B number used for U.S. export filing.
searchedAs: hs code for wooden furniture parts
hs code for office chair parts

faqs.question: What is the HS code for an office chair or a sofa?
faqs.answer: An office swivel chair with height adjustment is 9401.39 (9401.31 if of wood). An upholstered sofa or chair with a wooden frame is 9401.61 and one with a metal frame 9401.71. Office desks and cabinets are 9403.10 (metal) or 9403.30 (wood), and mattresses are 9404.21 or 9404.29.

faqs.question: What is the HS code for LED light fixtures?
faqs.answer: LED chandeliers and ceiling or wall fittings are 9405.11, LED table, desk and floor lamps 9405.21, and other LED luminaires 9405.42. Lamp parts are 9405.91 (glass), 9405.92 (plastic) and 9405.99 (other).
searchedAs: hs code for led lighting fixtures
hs code for ceiling light fixtures

faqs.question: What is the HS code for car seats and seat parts?
faqs.answer: Seats of a kind used in motor vehicles are 9401.20, aircraft seats 9401.10, and parts of seats 9401.99 (9401.91 if of wood). Seat parts, 9401.99, are the largest single U.S. Chapter 94 export line. For Russia and Belarus, motor-vehicle and aircraft seats need a BIS licence.
searchedAs: hs code for car seat parts
hs code for aircraft seat parts

faqs.question: What is Canada's steel derivative surtax, and does it hit U.S. prefabricated buildings?
faqs.answer: Yes. Since December 26, 2025 Canada's Steel Derivative Goods Surtax Order charges 25% on listed steel derivative goods from every country, the U.S. included. In Chapter 94 it covers steel modular building units (9406.20) and other prefabricated buildings (9406.90), metal office furniture (9403.10) and furniture parts other than of wood (9403.99); goods already under Canada's U.S. surtax do not pay it twice.
searchedAs: steel derivative goods surtax order canada

faqs.question: How much furniture does the U.S. export, and who buys it?
faqs.answer: The U.S. exported $9.41 billion of Chapter 94 goods in 2025, down 1.9% from 2024: $3.67 billion of seats and seat parts, $2.73 billion of furniture, $1.42 billion of lighting and $796 million of medical furniture. Canada bought 46% and Mexico 19%; the UK, the Netherlands, Japan and Germany follow at about 2–3% each.
